name: Carta de Ciudadanía (Ciudadanía Legal)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 3 years of habitual residence in Uruguay for applicants who have 'constituted family' (commonly understood as being married/in a registered partnership and/or having children), age 18+, able to speak Spanish, with proof of livelihood (employment, property, or business).
requirements.fix_path: Accrue 3 years of habitual residence while having constituted family.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 years of habitual residence in Uruguay for applicants without constituted family, age 18+, able to speak Spanish, with proof of livelihood.

evidence_required.document: Proof of nationality (birth certificate, marriage certificate, passport)
Residency certificate and migration movement records
Evidence of livelihood (employment history, property, or business registration)

sources.title: Sitio oficial de la República Oriental del Uruguay -- Carta de Ciudadanía: 3-year (family) / 5-year (without family) tracks, Spanish-language requirement, free processing, Corte Electoral administration

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Uruguay's initial build. Uruguay's citizenship system is structurally distinctive: this is 'legal citizenship' (as distinct from 'natural citizenship', see uy_citizenship_descent), granted administratively by the Corte Electoral (Electoral Court) based on constitutional criteria (Article 75), rather than a typical executive-branch naturalisation process -- processing is entirely FREE OF CHARGE, and no criminal record documentation is required from the applicant (the Court obtains checks directly). TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT RESIDENCE-LENGTH TRACKS (3yr with family / 5yr without) modelled as OR-logic groups within one process, confirmed directly at tier-1. The exact legal definition of 'family constituted' (constituir familia) -- e.g. whether unmarried cohabitation alone qualifies, or a specific marriage/registered-partnership status is required -- was not further detailed in the source fetched; treated at face value rather than narrowed by assumption. dual_citizenship_allowed set true: Uruguay does not require renouncing prior nationality for legal citizenship, unlike several other countries built in this dataset.
